data.long_meaning: Madan is a Sanskrit name, derived from the word 'mada' meaning intoxication or infatuation. In Hindu mythology, Madan is the god of love and desire, often depicted as riding on a chariot pulled by white horses. He is also known as Manmadh or Kamadeva. The name Madan carries the meaning “God of Love” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Madan usually hope their child will grow to embody god of love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
